whatItIs.text: Cream soured and thickened by lactic-acid bacteria — tangy, spoonable, and central to dips, baked potatoes, and Central European cooking.

historyNote.text: It began as thrift: the cream skimmed off milk was left to ferment at moderate temperature, the bacteria thickening and acidifying it — 'souring' being a natural way of preserving cream. US regulations require at least 18% milk fat before bulking.

howToChoose.text: Short ingredient lists (cream, culture) taste best; 'light' versions use thickeners to replace the fat's body. Check the pot date — it's a fresh product.

storage.text: Keep sealed in the fridge and use a clean spoon.

useItUp.text: Stir the last spoonfuls into scrambled eggs, soup, or a pan sauce; it also enriches cake batter and biscuit dough.

substitutions.note: richer, less sour; won't split in sauces
